tiles.title: A laptop-trained small model against one 14 times its size
tiles.plain: We gave 80 complaints it had never seen to our small model and to a much bigger one. Ours got 69 right, or correctly said "I can't tell". The big one, asked to do it alone, got 1.
tiles.detail: The small model is a 0.5-billion-parameter model with a 35 MB adapter, trained on this laptop's CPU. It only reads the facts; a verified library does the law, and a gate stops anything the library did not give. Invented provisions or dates in its output: 0.
tiles.failed: Three of its seven sealed claims failed and are kept: the reader got every fact exactly right on only 40 of 80; it abstained on 18 of 21 incomplete complaints (the bar was 19); and it proposed one angle where it did not apply.
tiles.notProve: One task (UK consumer claims), 80 synthetic complaints. 25 of the big model's answers came back empty from its runner; even if the four that later answered were all right it would reach 6.3%.

tiles.title: How much smaller two organs' messages get once they share a seed
tiles.plain: Our codec shrank a book of call records to under a fifteenth of its size, and gave back every byte exactly.
tiles.detail: LIGHT is one lossless codec with five layers of prediction. The fifth layer is shared context: the more two ends have already seen together, the less a new message costs.
tiles.failed: We sealed a claim of 15× before measuring. It came in at 14.827×, so that claim failed by 0.173 and stays failed. A second claim, that the layers' gains simply multiply, also failed.
tiles.notProve: That figure needs the shared seed. With no seed (a stranger's first message) LIGHT made the same call book 2.18× smaller, and Brotli beat it there. The table below shows every type, losses included.

tiles.title: 11,112 attempts to get past the door
tiles.plain: We threw forged, replayed, tampered and random messages at a signed door. Not one got through, nothing crashed, and all 100 genuine messages were delivered.
tiles.detail: Every refusal names the check that caught it. After one forgery was refused, 999 of 1,000 mutated copies of it were recognised on sight.
tiles.notProve: One door, in front of one deliberately naive program, against these attack classes. It is not a claim about every attack that exists.

receipt.label: receipt 24d8f269, and the full test to run yourself

tiles.title: Do the tests actually bite?
tiles.plain: We break our own code on purpose, one small change at a time, and count how many breaks the tests notice. A test suite that misses breaks is theatre.
tiles.detail: The grader behind every minted model: 425 of 426 broken copies caught, and the one survivor is published with its reason. The spend wall: 112 of 112. Kardlings: 1,518 of 1,518 across 29 modules, on GitHub's machines.
tiles.notProve: A high kill rate says the tests notice changes to the code. It does not say the code does the right thing for a case nobody thought to test.

receipt.label: the grader's kill rate, on every receipt it issues

tiles.title: Found in our own tools, by running them
tiles.plain: Our own quote checker once passed a fake quote: it found "he said yes" inside "she said yes". We caught it by feeding every tool one example of every kind of input, then fixed all three and wrote down what was wrong.
tiles.detail: CiteLock now needs whole words. Conform used to skip schema rules it did not understand and now refuses them out loud. GlyphGuard missed a block of look-alike mathematical letters and now catches it.
tiles.notProve: Three faults found is not zero faults left. It is the habit that matters: each tool had passed its own tests when these were found.

receipt.label: CiteLock, with the fault and the fix on the page

tiles.title: 60 hostile days against the spend wall
tiles.plain: An AI agent that can spend money needs a wall it cannot talk its way past. We simulated 60 days of at least double the demand. The budget was never exceeded.
tiles.detail: The wall sets aside a call's worst case before the call is made. The hard stop latched on day 40 and not one call passed after it. Calls with no evidence for needing the paid model were all refused.
tiles.notProve: A simulation, replayed through the real wall. The wall has not yet carried real spending: its key has never been installed, and the page says so.

receipt.label: the wall, its simulation and its audit

tiles.title: What the AI may not do alone
tiles.detail: Publishing, spending, deleting and anything that reaches a customer wait behind a human key. That is a rule in the code, not a promise in a brochure.
tiles.notProve: A count of the dispatcher's own policy on the date shown. It is a design rule, not a safety guarantee.
